Alabama State House: History, Structure, and Future Developments

The Alabama State House, located in Montgomery, Alabama, serves as the primary meeting place for the Alabama Legislature, housing both the Alabama Senate and the Alabama House of Representatives. While often confused with the Alabama State Capitol, the State House has been the center of legislative activity since 1985.

History of the Alabama State House

The Alabama State House was originally constructed in 1963 as the Alabama Highway Department Building. It was primarily used by the Alabama Department of Transportation (formerly the Alabama State Highway Department). However, in 1985, legislative sessions were moved from the Alabama State Capitol to the State House to accommodate renovation efforts.

Although these renovations were completed in 1992, the Legislature continued to meet in the State House, which was officially renamed following the 1985 move. Originally, the 5th through 7th floors were designated for the Legislature, but due to increasing space demands, an eighth floor was later added.

Structure and Usage

The Alabama State House is a seven-story building with an additional basement level. Each floor serves specific governmental purposes:

  • Basement (First Floor) – Used for committee rooms and miscellaneous offices.
  • Second Floor – Houses the Governor’s Legislative Office and Alabama Budget Office.
  • Third Floor – Home to the Attorney General’s Office.
  • Fifth & Sixth Floors – Exclusively used by the House of Representatives.
  • Seventh & Eighth Floors – Dedicated to the Alabama Senate.
  • The Lieutenant Governor’s Office is located on the seventh floor.

Plans for a New Alabama State House

Over the years, concerns have been raised about structural issues, lack of space, and accessibility challenges at the Alabama State House. As a result, proposals for a new legislative facility have been under discussion for decades.

Past Proposals

  • In 2009, legislators debated constructing a new facility on Dexter Avenue to create a government mall, though this plan was ultimately abandoned.
  • In 2020, Senator Del Marsh proposed using $200 million in CARES Act funding for a new State House, but public opposition led to the proposal’s withdrawal.

Current Plans (2023-2027)

In 2023, the Alabama Legislature approved the construction of a new State House to address aging infrastructure and space constraints. The project is being designed by Goodwyn Mills Cawood in collaboration with Robert A.M. Stern Architects.

  • Funding: The $400 million project is being financed by the Retirement Systems of Alabama (RSA).
  • Timeline: Construction began in late 2023 and is expected to be completed by 2026.
  • Relocation: The Legislature is anticipated to move into the new State House by 2027.

The Alabama State Legislature

The Alabama Legislature is a bicameral body consisting of the Alabama House of Representatives and the Alabama State Senate. It is responsible for passing state laws, approving budgets, and overseeing the executive branch.

Alabama State Senate

  • Total Members: 35
  • Term Length: 4 years
  • Current Partisan Composition:
    • Republicans: 26
    • Democrats: 8
    • Vacancies: 1
  • Senate President: Lieutenant Governor Will Ainsworth (R)

Alabama House of Representatives

  • Total Members: 105
  • Term Length: 4 years
  • Current Partisan Composition:
    • Republicans: 76
    • Democrats: 29
  • House Speaker: Nathaniel Ledbetter (R)

Conclusion

The Alabama State House has served as the home of the Alabama Legislature since 1985, despite originally being a transportation department building. While it has undergone several changes, increasing space constraints, structural concerns, and modernization needs have led to the approval of a new State House, expected to be completed by 2026.

As Alabama continues to grow, the Legislature’s move into a modern facility will ensure better efficiency, accessibility, and functionality for state governance.
